paragraphs.title: An Inner Call to Praise and Remember Goodness

answers: To his soul
To the angels
To the oppressed
easy.explanation: He says, “Bless the LORD, O my soul.”
easy.q: To whom does David speak at the beginning of the psalm?

answers: Moses’ ways
All the LORD’s benefits
The length of human life
easy.explanation: Verse 2 says, “forget not all his benefits.”
easy.q: What does David tell his soul not to forget?

answers: He reveals His throne
He punishes every person
He forgives, heals, and redeems
easy.explanation: The verses mention forgiveness, healing, redemption, mercy, and renewal.
easy.q: What does the LORD do in these opening verses?

answers: To remember the good things the LORD gives
To describe human life as grass
To command the angels to obey
medium.explanation: The call to praise is connected with remembering the LORD’s benefits.
medium.q: Why does David call upon his soul to bless the LORD?

answers: A throne, angels, and a covenant
Forgiveness, healing, redemption, mercy, and renewal
Sin, punishment, death, and forgetfulness
medium.explanation: These verses list forgiveness, healing, redemption, lovingkindness, tender mercies, and renewed youth.
medium.q: Which sequence of benefits appears in verses 3–5?

answers: He punishes with evil
He hides what is good
He fills a person with good things
medium.explanation: The statement describes the LORD as providing abundance and goodness.
medium.q: What does “Who satisfieth thy mouth with good things” mean?

answers: The following verses explain the benefits that must be remembered
The list cancels the call to praise
The list concerns only angels
challenge.explanation: The next verses identify the LORD’s benefits, including forgiveness, healing, and redemption.
challenge.q: How does “forget not all his benefits” relate to the list that follows?

answers: Praise is intended only for the body
Praise should come from the whole inner person
People should forget the LORD’s benefits
challenge.explanation: The phrase calls for wholehearted and inward praise.
challenge.q: What is emphasized by the words “all that is within me”?

answers: The LORD gives deliverance and fresh goodness
Human life passes quickly
Angels obey with a loud voice
challenge.explanation: The verses present the LORD as one who rescues, blesses, and renews life.
challenge.q: What idea connects redemption, lovingkindness, and renewed youth?

paragraphs.title: God’s Justice and Compassion toward the Oppressed and Sinful

answers: For angels only
For all that are oppressed
For people of the earliest generations only
easy.explanation: Verse 6 says that He executes righteousness and judgment “for all that are oppressed.”
easy.q: For whom does the LORD execute righteousness and judgment?

answers: Merciful and gracious
Forgetful and hasty
Weak and hidden
easy.explanation: He is called “merciful and gracious, slow to anger, and plenteous in mercy.”
easy.q: Which qualities are attributed to the LORD?

answers: He will not make His ways known
He will not pity those who fear Him
He will not always chide or keep His anger forever
easy.explanation: Verse 9 says, “He will not always chide: neither will he keep his anger for ever.”
easy.q: What will the LORD not do forever?

answers: Because He knows their frame and remembers that they are dust
Because they are not human
Because their lives last forever
medium.explanation: The LORD remembers human weakness and that people are dust.
medium.q: Why does the LORD pity those who fear Him?

answers: As high as heaven is above earth
As far as the east is from the west
As far as one mountain is from another
medium.explanation: Verse 12 says, “As far as the east is from the west.”
medium.q: How far does the LORD remove transgressions from His people?

answers: Those who have been afflicted or wronged
Those who serve the LORD
Those who live in heaven
medium.explanation: The oppressed are people who suffer affliction or injustice.
medium.q: What does “all that are oppressed” refer to in this passage?

answers: Anger and punishment are not the whole of His relationship with people
The LORD never executes judgment
Human beings never sin
challenge.explanation: The passage places judgment alongside patience, forgiveness, and compassion.
challenge.q: What does the contrast between “not always chide” and the LORD’s mercy teach?

answers: It presents complete distance
It portrays mercy as close and personal
It removes the reality of human weakness
challenge.explanation: The LORD’s pity is compared with a father’s compassion for his children.
challenge.q: How does the image of a father and children deepen the description of mercy?

answers: Recognizing human weakness explains the LORD’s compassion and patience
Knowing human weakness causes Him only to forget sins
There is no connection between the ideas
challenge.explanation: The verses connect the LORD’s knowledge of human frailty with His pity.
challenge.q: What connection exists between knowing our frame and not keeping anger forever?

paragraphs.title: Human Frailty versus the Everlasting Kindness of God

answers: A throne in heaven
Grass and a flower
The hosts of angels
easy.explanation: Human days are compared with grass and a flower of the field.
easy.q: What is human life compared to?

answers: It becomes everlasting
It becomes a throne
It is gone, and its place is known no more
easy.explanation: The verse uses the fading flower to picture the brevity of human life.
easy.q: What happens to the flower when the wind passes over it?

answers: Those who fear Him
The oppressed only
Angels only
easy.explanation: Verse 17 says His mercy is upon “them that fear him.”
easy.q: Upon whom is the mercy of the LORD from everlasting to everlasting?

answers: Human life passes away, but the LORD’s mercy continues forever
Angels are different from the oppressed
The east is different from the west
medium.explanation: Human life is brief, while the LORD’s mercy and righteousness endure.
medium.q: What is the central contrast in verses 15–18?

answers: Children’s children
The grass of the field
Everyone who rejects His commandments
medium.explanation: Verse 17 says His righteousness is “unto children’s children.”
medium.q: To whom does the LORD’s righteousness continue in future generations?

answers: Forget His commandments
Remember them in order to do them
Avoid every commandment
medium.explanation: Verse 18 speaks of those who remember His commandments “to do them.”
medium.q: What do those who keep the covenant and remember the commandments do?

answers: It highlights human frailty in contrast with the lasting mercy of God
It proves that people control everything
It describes the power of angels
challenge.explanation: The shortness of human life makes the enduring mercy of the LORD especially significant.
challenge.q: Why does comparing people to grass and flowers emphasize the importance of the LORD’s mercy?

answers: Keeping His covenant and remembering His commandments
Avoiding judgment
Forgetting past actions
challenge.explanation: The passage refers to those who keep His covenant and remember His commandments to do them.
challenge.q: What responsibility is mentioned alongside the LORD’s everlasting mercy?

answers: Both last for the same short time
The LORD’s mercy extends far beyond the length of human life
Human beings become part of heaven
challenge.explanation: The everlasting duration of God’s mercy contrasts with the temporary nature of human life.
challenge.q: What does the comparison between “everlasting to everlasting” and human life mean?

paragraphs.title: God’s Kingdom over the Heavens and All Reality

answers: In the heavens
In the field
In the east
easy.explanation: Verse 19 says, “The LORD hath prepared his throne in the heavens.”
easy.q: Where has the LORD prepared His throne?

answers: It rules over all
It disappears from the world
It belongs only to humanity
easy.explanation: The verse says, “his kingdom ruleth over all.”
easy.q: What does the LORD’s kingdom do?

answers: Human weakness
The LORD’s kingdom and authority
The brief life of a flower
easy.explanation: A throne represents royal authority and rule.
easy.q: What does the throne represent in this verse?

answers: The throne in the heavens is connected with a kingdom ruling over all
The heavens are separated from every kingdom
The verse does not mention the world
medium.explanation: The heavenly throne is presented together with the kingdom’s universal rule.
medium.q: What connection does the verse make between the heavens and all reality?

answers: The kingdom rules in only one place
The kingdom rules over every part of reality
The kingdom belongs only to angels
medium.q: What does “ruleth over all” mean in this verse?

answers: It moves from human life to the LORD’s rule over everything
It returns only to the flower
It describes only human weakness
medium.explanation: The verse presents the LORD as ruler over all creation.
medium.q: How does this verse expand the psalm’s focus from people to the whole world?

answers: The verse emphasizes authority and rule
The verse concerns only healing
The verse denies the existence of a kingdom
challenge.explanation: Both “throne” and “kingdom” are terms of royal authority.
challenge.q: What is suggested by the combination of “throne” and “kingdom”?

answers: The heavens only
The earth only
All things
challenge.explanation: The verse explicitly says that His kingdom rules “over all.”
challenge.q: What is the extent of the LORD’s kingdom according to the verse?

answers: It presents the universal King whom all are called to bless
It describes the forgetting of benefits
It focuses only on the brevity of human life
challenge.explanation: After declaring the LORD’s universal rule, the psalm calls angels and all creation to bless Him.
challenge.q: How does verse 19 prepare for the call to praise in the following verses?

paragraphs.title: Universal Praise from Angels and All Creation

answers: The angels
The oppressed alone
The flowers
easy.explanation: Verse 20 addresses the angels of the LORD.
easy.q: Who is called to bless the LORD at the beginning of this section?

answers: They do His pleasure
They forget His commandments
They hide His kingdom
easy.explanation: Verse 21 calls them “ministers of his, that do his pleasure.”
easy.q: What do the LORD’s ministers do?

answers: His soul
Moses alone
The oppressed alone
easy.explanation: The psalm ends with “Bless the LORD, O my soul.”
easy.q: Whom does David invite to join at the end?

answers: The angels act according to the word of the LORD
The angels ignore the LORD’s word
The passage connects the ideas in no way
medium.explanation: The angels are described as doing His commandments and listening to the voice of His word.
medium.q: What connection exists between doing God’s commandments and hearkening to His word?

answers: Angels, hosts, ministers, and all His works
The oppressed, sinners, flowers, and thrones
Moses, Israel, the east, and the west
medium.explanation: The call expands from angels to His hosts, ministers, and all His works.
medium.q: Which sequence of groups is called to bless the LORD?

answers: To join personal praise with the praise of all creation
To cancel the praise of the other creatures
To describe the brevity of human life
medium.explanation: David adds his own personal praise to the universal call to bless the LORD.
medium.q: Why does the conclusion return to David’s soul?

answers: From the angels to all creation
From all creation to one person only
From judgment to sin alone
challenge.explanation: The passage includes angels, hosts, ministers, and all the LORD’s works.
challenge.q: How does the scope of praise expand throughout this section?

answers: Praise is connected with obedience to God’s will
Praise replaces obedience
Actions and praise are unrelated
challenge.explanation: The verses join worship with carrying out the LORD’s commandments and pleasure.
challenge.q: What does the combination of blessing the LORD and doing His pleasure teach?

answers: Both call David’s soul to bless the LORD
Both compare human life to grass
Both mention only the oppressed
challenge.explanation: The psalm begins and ends with the call, “Bless the LORD, O my soul.”
challenge.q: How does the ending connect with the beginning of the psalm?
